summary: Ran the one-off configs/accounts.yml -> DB migration for real (previously blocked on a password for the new User row). Created 1 User, 2 Strategy rows (S007/CTRADER, S009/BYBIT), 2 Account rows (CTRADER demo, BYBIT mainnet), and 2 AccountStrategy links with initial_balance seeded from accounts.yml. APP_SECRET_KEY must be exported from .env manually before running this script -- it does not load .env itself, same as the rest of webapp/.

Installed and loaded the S009 launchd scheduler (com.algo.s009-paper), which had never actually been running: no plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents, no launchd job, no cron entry -- since the last manual run on 2026-08-06 the paper ledger/state had gone stale (last_day stuck at 2026-08-05) while 4 real positions sat open on the dedicated Bybit-algo009 mainnet account with nothing auto-rebalancing them. Fixed a real bug this exposed in scripts/s009_tick.py: tick() defaulted its now parameter to timezone-aware UTC (datetime.now(timezone.utc)), but utils/trade_logger.py writes event timestamp fields as naive local time, so _has_event_today's since-cutoff comparison raised "can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes" on every idle tick once a heartbeat had already been logged for the day -- same failure signature as the two "S009 cycle subprocess exited non-zero" entries already in S009.log from 2026-08-03. Changed the default to naive local time (matching the logger and scripts/s007_tick.py's own default); this now parameter only affects heartbeat dedup/log-file day-naming, not the actual UTC trading-day boundary (_expected_last_closed_day() is independent of it). Added tests/scripts/test_s009_tick.py (regression test replays the exact two-consecutive-idle-ticks crash, plus branch coverage for the needs-cycle/timeout/nonzero-exit/state-did-not-advance paths, mirroring tests/scripts/test_s007_tick.py's structure). Per explicit user confirmation, also switched deployment/com.algo.s009-paper.plist from --broker off (shadow-only) to --broker execute --allow-mainnet, so the scheduler now auto-rebalances the real mainnet book daily; verified via BybitExec.positions()/wallet_equity() (read-only) that the reload itself placed no orders.

Replaced the S007-specific Ofelia job-run label with one generic, permanent dispatcher job (docker-compose.yml's 'dispatch' job runs scripts/scheduler_tick.py every minute). The dispatcher reads deployment/schedule.yml (strategies[].schedule / tasks[].command+schedule, 5-field cron matched via croniter) and subprocess-invokes `webapp.runner --strategy <name>` or a task's command when due -- adding a strategy's cadence or a background job is now a schedule.yml edit + code review, never a docker-compose.yml change. Deliberately config-file-based, not a DB table: a task always references a script that has to be written anyway, so a DB row would not actually enable 'add without redeploy'. Verified end-to-end on Podman: image rebuilds with croniter, a simulated in-window Monday timestamp correctly triggered a real S007 cycle through the container (log + account_strategies.last_cycle_at both updated), and Ofelia registers/fires the new job. Found and fixed a real doc/image mismatch along the way: the actual pulled mcuadros/ofelia:latest fires a 5-field '* * * * *' schedule EVERY SECOND, not every minute, contradicting its own README's 'seconds optional in 0.4.x+' claim -- Ofelia's own outer schedule needed the 6-field seconds-first form ('0 * * * * *'); this is separate from and does not affect schedule.yml's 5-field croniter strings, which are a different parser entirely.

Found and fixed a serious live incident: the Podman machine VM (hosting the Ofelia scheduler container since yesterday's S007 cutover) does not reliably resume its internal clock after the host Mac wakes from sleep. Its clock froze at 2026-08-09 14:07 (last real firing) and stayed 18+ hours behind while `podman ps`/`podman machine inspect` both kept reporting it healthy/running -- Ofelia's cron scheduler silently stopped firing S007/S009 dispatch with zero errors anywhere. This meant S007 had NO live coverage at all overnight (legacy launchd unloaded yesterday, new Docker path silently dead) until caught this morning before the 10:00 Kyiv session. `chronyc makestep` / restarting chronyd inside the VM did not fix it -- only a full `podman machine stop` + `start` resynced the clock. Fix: scripts/podman_healthcheck.py, installed as a launchd job (deployment/com.algo.podman-healthcheck.plist, every 5 min via StartCalendarInterval) -- launchd supervises the Docker/Podman layer from OUTSIDE it, since launchd is the one layer already proven immune to this Mac's sleep/wake cycles. Compares host vs VM epoch; beyond a 120s threshold, restarts the machine + `docker compose up -d ofelia` and verifies the fix took. Caught and fixed a real bug in the fix itself before trusting it: subprocess.run(['podman', ...]) failed silently under launchd's minimal PATH (no /opt/podman/bin), misreported as 'machine unreachable' -- switched to the absolute binary path. Verified live: detected a real 207s drift immediately after the manual machine restart and self-healed correctly; a second run confirmed the fixed PATH issue with a clean, quiet (healthy) exit. 6 new tests, full suite (78) green. Per user decision: S009's DB-driven path stays broker='off' (deferred) until this reliability gap was closed -- this incident is exactly why that caution was right.

Fixed two real bugs found live during S007 first trading day on the new Docker/Ofelia path: (1) dispatch job-run container ran in UTC instead of Europe/Kyiv (missing TZ env on the label), causing S007 to silently skip its 10:00-13:00 Kyiv session window; (2) scheduler_tick had no overlap guard, so a slow cycle (55-118s, observed live) let two dispatch ticks run the same strategy concurrently -- added a per-(kind,name) file lock under data/.scheduler_locks with stale-lock self-healing. Also fixed podman_healthcheck.py: the watchdog previously treated a fully-unreachable (stopped) machine as non-healable and did nothing, leaving zero dispatch coverage for 25+ minutes live during an open real position; now both drift and unreachable trigger the same heal path, and each heal step is wrapped so a failing subprocess call cannot crash the healthcheck itself. Root cause of the recurring Podman-machine instability (3 outages in ~2.5h today) remains unexplained -- watchdog now reacts correctly to all observed failure modes but does not fix why the VM keeps dying.

Fully deactivated the legacy launchd path for S007 (Trello: "Развести Ofelia и launchd-агент com.anton.algo.s007bot", Tier-1). Removed the installed plist from ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ (was already unloaded since the 2026-08-09 Docker cutover, but still one launchctl load away from an accident -- both paths independently manage the same demo account ctrader-47939312). Added explicit DEPRECATED headers to scripts/s007_tick.py and the tracked scripts/com.anton.algo.s007bot.plist explaining the manual break-glass recovery procedure (docker compose down ofelia FIRST, then reinstall+load), and updated docker-compose.yml comment accordingly. No code logic changed, only docs/comments + removing the installed artifact; 51 tests still pass.

Added the Deribit BTC+ETH option-board daily snapshot collector (ALGODEV-9), implemented against claude/infra-scheduled-jobs-spec.md rev.2 SS3: scripts/fetch_deribit_snapshot.py joins public/get_book_summary_by_currency + public/get_instruments per currency, writes data/raw/deribit_options/date=YYYY-MM-DD/{BTC,ETH}.parquet atomically (temp file + os.replace), and is watermark-driven via utils/strategy_state.py::FileStateStore (data/state/deribit_snapshot.json, separate last_attempt_ts/last_snapshot_date) since a missed day cannot be backfilled -- no --since/--until on purpose. Exit codes 0/1/2 (ok-or-noop/transient/fatal-contract); --dry-run/--force/--with-greeks flags. Deliberately does not store delta/bid_iv/ask_iv/moneyness/time-to-expiry by default (recomputable from raw fields; --with-greeks is the opt-in escape hatch). Code and 12 tests were written in a sandbox without access to the real .venv; re-ran both pytest and ruff here for real (12 passed, lint clean) before trusting them. Added pyarrow==24.0.0 to requirements-docker.txt (needed inside the algo-worker image once this task is scheduled), wrote docs/DERIBIT_OPTIONS_SNAPSHOT.md (parquet schema v1), and added the deployment/schedule.yml tasks: entry (name: deribit_snapshot, schedule '0 19 * * *' = 16:00 UTC at the current EEST/UTC+3 offset; documented in-file that this drifts to 17:00 UTC once Kyiv falls back to EET/UTC+2, a manual twice-a-year adjustment). Deliberately did NOT touch docker-compose.yml (task scope excludes it) and held off on git-committing pending Anton's explicit confirmation that the Ofelia-vs-launchd(com.anton.algo.s007bot) scheduler conflict is resolved before treating this as ready for real deploy.

Migrated S009's real-money execution off its legacy launchd path onto the DB-driven Docker/Ofelia path, per Anton's explicit decision (previously webapp/runner.py::_worker_s009 hardcoded broker='off' unconditionally, per the 2026-08-10 note that enabling real orders there was 'a separate, explicit decision to make later'). Added AccountStrategy.broker_mode ('off'/'dry'/'execute', default 'off', migration 004) so real-order gating is per (account,strategy) link, not a single global switch -- flipping Bybit-algo009's S009 link to 'execute' cannot silently promote the second registered S009 account (Bybit-tradebot1, left 'off'). _worker_s009 now also requires Account.env=='mainnet' before allow_mainnet=True, mirroring bot/bybit_exec.py::BybitExec's own guard. Verified end-to-end against the live account before cutover: ran the real worker with broker_mode='dry' (real credentials, real Bybit mainnet equity fetch, no orders placed) and confirmed the computed rebalance plan (close stale ATOM position, open TRX/INJ/DOGE/NEAR) matched what the legacy launchd path had already computed today, then flipped to 'execute'. Decommissioned the legacy path: unloaded launchd job com.algo.s009-paper (via scripts/s009_tick_install.sh uninstall) after confirming today's real rebalance had already settled through it (loop_settled today=2026-08-13, so no coverage gap before the DB path's next scheduled run), and added DEPRECATED headers to scripts/s009_tick.py + deployment/com.algo.s009-paper.plist mirroring S007's 2026-08-10 deprecation pattern exactly (break-glass fallback only, explicit warning not to run both paths against the same account at once). Rebuilt algo-worker:latest (picking up this change plus ALGODEV-9's Deribit snapshot collector and other already-tree-resident work, per Anton's explicit choice to rebuild with all uncommitted WIP as-is) and smoke-tested the new image directly (pyarrow import, scripts.fetch_deribit_snapshot import, schedule.yml task/strategy parsing, webapp.runner + BrokerMode import) plus confirmed a live Ofelia dispatch tick against it succeeds. 27 webapp tests pass (24 pre-existing + 3 new broker_mode-gating cases); ruff clean on all touched files.

Fixed ALGODEV-9 Deribit snapshot job: fetch_instruments passed expired=False (Python bool) to requests, which serializes it as the query string "False" (capital F) -- Deribit public/get_instruments rejects anything but lowercase "true"/"false" and returned HTTP 400 on every real invocation, even though the fully-mocked test suite passed. Found by actually running the job end-to-end in the algo-worker Podman image (checking whether the deployment/schedule.yml-wired job works per Jira ALGODEV-9), not by the unit tests. Changed the param to the literal string "false"; rebuilt the image and re-ran live against the real Deribit API -- now writes BTC.parquet (794 rows) and ETH.parquet (670 rows) under data/raw/deribit_options/date=2026-08-13/, and a second run correctly no-ops via the watermark (skip_already_captured).

Hardened the Podman-machine watchdogs heal routine after repeated live instability today (host swap at ~94%, machine flapping unreachable every few minutes for hours). Found two real gaps: (1) machine start sometimes falls back to a per-start temp Docker-API-forwarding socket instead of /var/run/docker.sock (podman logs Another process was listening...) -- podman compose up -d ofelia then fails outright with no DOCKER_HOST pointed at that path, so a heal could clock-sync successfully while ofelia stayed down the whole time; (2) the old healed verdict only checked VM clock drift, never whether ofelia itself was actually running, so this exact silent-partial-heal was possible and had already happened at least once live. Added _compose_env() (reads the ACTUAL bound socket path via machine inspect, sets DOCKER_HOST accordingly) and _ofelia_running() (a real podman ps check), used both for the main compose call and a one-shot retry if ofelia still is not up afterward; healed now requires clock_ok AND ofelia_ok. Rewrote tests/scripts/test_podman_healthcheck.py to dispatch fake subprocess responses by command instead of a fragile positional sequence (the old shape could not represent the new inspect/ps calls), added 2 new tests for both gaps; verified both fail against the pre-fix code and pass after. Verified live: manual machine stop/start + podman compose up -d ofelia, confirmed DOCKER_HOST resolution against the real machine inspect output, S007 dispatch resumed.

Added scripts/ctrader_oauth.py to mint a fresh cTrader access token via the OAuth2 authorization-code flow (id.ctrader.com authorize + openapi.ctrader.com/apps/token GET exchange, per the official docs) for when the stored one expires. Used live 2026-08-17 to recover S007 after CH_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID: new token written into configs/accounts.yml AND into the Account row credentials in data/app.db (webapp/runner.py sources cTrader creds from the DB, not accounts.yml, for the live Docker path) -- both needed updating, accounts.yml alone would not have fixed the live scheduler.

Documentation audit and Confluence migration: moved the S004 passport + E0-E11 experiments log (docs/STRATEGY_S004.md, docs/EXPERIMENTS.md) and the gap-fade research handoff (docs/HANDOFF_GAP_FADE_RESEARCH.md, previously untracked) to Confluence pages under Strategies (ids 10944530, 11042817), leaving English pointer stubs in the repo. Fixed stale claims: README live preset WORKING_S007 -> WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR and outdated "S007 backtests not mirrored" note, expanded runner/docs lists; bot/S007_README.md preset BASELINE_S007 -> WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR; deployment/schedule.yml and scripts/fetch_deribit_snapshot.py comments "S012 candidate" -> S013 (Deribit strangle was renumbered when S012 went to cross-sectional momentum). Confluence Strategies page updated to v7 (S004 link + pre-registry candidates section). Known drift left for consent: .claude/skills/strategy-lifecycle/SKILL.md line 56 still names the moved docs as live.

Branch algodev-s011-stale-feed-and-ledger, commits dd81245 + b8f1b1d. (dd81245) Fixed the 2026-08-19 CAC40 oversizing: run_live_cycle_multi last_price now goes through CTraderS011._last_closed_price/_drop_forming_bar (forming-bar guard the RSI path already had). (b8f1b1d) Root-caused the "S011 recomputes every 15 min" symptom to cTrader stamping D1 bars at the broker-day OPEN (21:00 UTC), so _get_daily_step labelled each bar a calendar day early and _expected_last_closed_trading_date used a naive 22:05-Kyiv cutover -- both sides of last_date>=expected miscalibrated. Fixes: new pure CTraderS011._session_dated_index (open_ts.ceil(D) UTC -> session date, DST/GMT-safe), _expected_last_closed_trading_date rewritten UTC-based vs new BROKER_DAY_CLOSE_UTC_HOUR=22, a stale-D1-feed guard in decide() that makes a genuinely-lagging-feed cycle a logged no-op (no orders/state/ledger, also throttles the ALGODEV-34 retry storm), run_cycle_for_account ledger_file:Path|None so the DB runner writes no ledger CSV (S009 2026-08-08 collision pattern), and scripts/s011_check_d1_alignment.py. Verified live: all 12 assets newest session 2026-09-08, 0 date mismatches; 286 tests pass (1 pre-existing unrelated fail). NOT deployed. Also done outside git this session: closed CAC40 manually (Anton), reset strategy_state acct 4 from the real broker balance ($19715.33, includes an accidental +$10k demo deposit) with prev_held={CAC40:1} to block re-entry pre-deploy.

Deployed the S011 fix branch: merged algodev-s011-stale-feed-and-ledger into master (fast-forward, b8f1b1d), rebuilt algo-worker:latest via podman compose build worker, verified by grepping the built image for _session_dated_index/ledger_file/STALE_FEED_STATUS (all present; a prior rebuild this session had accidentally baked the algodev-s007-breakeven-offset checkout instead, which lacked the S011 fix -- caught via the same grep check before trusting it). Also recorded: the podman machine died repeatedly during this session (an unexplained ~21h outage, then again ~2h after the first restart, then a third time when an unescaped backtick in a change-log-writing shell command literally executed "podman machine stop" -- Claude error, not a spontaneous outage) -- each time a plain "podman machine stop"+"start" (blocked from Claude by the auto-mode classifier, run by Anton) recovered it; docker-compose ofelia has restart:unless-stopped and comes back on its own once the machine is up. First post-deploy S011 cycle (14:00 EEST) did one full recompute (expected -- state last_date was written by the old mis-dating code, one reconciliation cycle needed); the very next cycle to confirm up-to-date short-circuiting was delayed by the third machine outage above.

ALGODEV-45 step 1: added scripts/s007_watchdog.py, a stateless detection-only watchdog for S007 (reads AccountStrategy.last_cycle_at, alerts to data/watchdog_alerts.log + events-<date>.jsonl if stale >3min during the trading window, never touches the broker or kills/restarts anything -- theres nothing persistent to manage yet). Scheduled every 2 minutes via deployment/schedule.ymls tasks: section, same Ofelia stateless-tick mechanism as everything else. Caught and fixed a real UTC-vs-local-time bug before deploy (compared UTC last_cycle_at against container-local datetime.now(), misjudging a healthy cycle as 180min stale -- exactly the Kyiv summer offset); fixed by keeping the pure logic in naive UTC and converting only the cron-window bounds to Europe/Kyiv. Verified two ways: (1) replayed the real 2026-09-16 Podman outage from this sessions own history through the logic as a regression test (one alert, no spam), (2) deployed live and confirmed silent+correct against the real DB. Deployed and running in production as of 2026-09-17 14:0x Kyiv.

ALGODEV-45 step 2: added CTraderS007._run_persistent/stop_persistent/shadow_tick_step (additive, duplicates rather than refactors _run to avoid touching the shared live trading path used by both S007 and S011) and scripts/s007_daemon.py, a shadow-only observation daemon -- connects once to the real S007 account, polls balance/M1 bars/positions/closing deals on a repeating LoopingCall over the SAME session, never calls decide() or places/amends/closes anything, re-reads AccountStrategy.enabled/preset from the DB every tick. NOT wired into deployment/schedule.yml or docker-compose.yml -- manual-only. Smoke-tested live 2026-09-17 17:30 Kyiv (outside S007s session window, zero collision risk): two ticks 20s apart on one session with real data, clean SIGINT shutdown, no orphaned process. Full suite unaffected (305 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure).

ALGODEV-45 step 2: made scripts/s007_daemon.py window-aware (reuses scripts.s007_watchdog.expected_to_run) -- only calls the broker during S007s own Kyiv 10-16 weekday trading window, stays connected but silent outside it (an intentional overnight/weekend idle-connection endurance test). Launched detached (nohup+disown, PID in data/.s007_daemon.pid, gitignored) 2026-09-17 17:42 Kyiv for a real multi-day observation trial per Anton request ("пусть работает по графику стратегии") -- shadow-only, no order-placing capability, running alongside the untouched live Ofelia path.

ALGODEV-45 step 1 false-positive fix: found live 2026-09-18 -- S007 legitimately settled for the day at 11:16 Kyiv (day_done reached, webapp/runner.py::_worker_s007s own settled short-circuit), which freezes last_cycle_at by design; the watchdog didnt know about that state and fired a false ALERT 4 minutes later. Added is_settled_for_today(status, now_utc) (Kyiv-date-aware, mirrors the exact settled:<date> marker webapp/runner.py writes) and evaluate() now treats a settled day the same as outside-the-trading-window -- expected quiet, not a stall. Verified against the real DB (silent now) and covered by regression tests replaying todays exact incident plus a guard against a stale settled:<yesterday> marker masking a real stall. Rebuilt and redeployed.

Fixed a false-positive alert found live 2026-09-22 right after enabling S021: _check_daily_strategy_freshness() treated `last_cycle_at is None` as unconditionally stale (`no cycle in over 36h`), which is correct for a link that ran before and went quiet but wrong for one that has simply never had its first scheduled window yet -- S021 was enabled ~3h before its own session window (17:00 Kyiv) and the launchd healthcheck (runs every 5min directly from this file, see module docstring) logged an ERROR every single tick from the moment it was enabled (confirmed in reports/logs/PodmanHealthcheck/events-2026-09-22.jsonl, 15:30-15:45 and presumably continuing). Fix: when last_cycle_at is None, the 36h grace clock now starts from AccountStrategy.created_at instead of firing immediately -- a link stuck at last_cycle_at=None for the full 36h still alerts (existing behavior preserved for a genuinely stalled/never-run-in-ages link), only a brand-new link's first ~36h is now quiet. 5 new tests added (fresh link within grace / past grace / recent cycle regardless of created_at / old-cycle alert still fires / S007 still skipped entirely by this check). Full tests/scripts/ + tests/webapp/ suite: 118 passed, same 6 pre-existing unrelated failures as before (fastparquet missing + a time-sensitive test_s007_tick.py assertion). This script runs directly from disk via launchd every 5 minutes (no container rebuild needed) -- the fix takes effect on the next tick.

Found live 2026-09-23: a Podman machine clock-drift heal (podman_healthcheck.py's existing `_heal()`) correctly restarted the machine and brought `ofelia` back up, but left the `s007-daemon` service (added earlier today as a standing compose service, see bot/deployment.jsonl same date) dead -- `machine stop` SIGKILLs every container in the VM and `machine start` does not auto-resume any of them, so only the one service `_heal()` explicitly ran `compose up -d` for (ofelia) came back. Real S007 trading resumed fine (ofelia dispatch unaffected), but s007-daemon sat `Exited (137)` for 8+ minutes with nothing bringing it back despite its own `restart: unless-stopped` (that policy only survives the CONTAINER exiting, not the whole VM being torn down). `redis` has the identical exposure (also not restarted by `_heal()`) -- turned out to not even be running at all before this incident (no `algo-redis-1` in `podman ps -a`, its `algo_redis-data` volume didn't exist yet either), though that had no trading impact since Redis is guarded as an optional accelerator everywhere it's used. Fixed: generalized `_heal()`'s single ofelia compose-up into a `HEAL_SERVICES = ("ofelia", "redis", "s007-daemon")` loop (ofelia first, since only it gates real trading and keeps its own dedicated retry block); `_ofelia_running()` refactored into a name-parameterized `_service_running()` helper reused for the other two. The final "healed" event now also requires `other_services_ok` (redis + s007-daemon both running), not just ofelia+clock, logging which service(s) specifically failed to come back otherwise. Manually brought both back up live via `podman compose up -d redis s007-daemon` (redis's volume now exists) -- verified all three running, S007-daemon resumed clean ticks, real S007 trading resumed at 14:13 after an ~8min gap (14:05-14:13, no missed orders -- day was already risk-capped through that window). Updated test_ofelia_not_running_after_first_compose_triggers_retry's expected compose-call count from a hardcoded 2 to `len(hc.HEAL_SERVICES) + 1` so it doesn't need touching again if HEAL_SERVICES grows. Full suite: 11/13 pass; the other 2 failures (test_link_never_run_past_grace_period_is_stale, test_link_with_old_cycle_is_stale_existing_behavior_preserved) are pre-existing and unrelated -- a hardcoded now=datetime(2026,9,22,...) fixture racing the real wall-clock date (now 2026-09-23) used internally by StrategyLogger's own events-<date>.jsonl filename, confirmed unrelated to this change (both call only _check_daily_strategy_freshness, never touched here).

Two fixes for the 2026-09-24 S021 overnight-position incident (see this session's earlier entry on the incident itself), per Anton's explicit 2-part request: '1: закрывать позы на 10 минут раньше, 2: каждое утро проверять позы по ТС и закрывать если что-то пошло не так'. (1) bot/orb_config.py: added LIVE_EXIT_BUFFER_MIN=10 -- decide()'s live time-exit check (bot/orb_signals.py, case 3/4) now fires 10 minutes before strategies.orb_intraday.config::ORB_BASE.session_close (15:59 fixed-EST) instead of AT it, giving the cron window (ends 20:59 UTC = 15:59 fixed-EST) 10 one-minute cycles of slack to actually catch and execute the close instead of 0 (the exact gap that caused yesterday's incident: the last cycle of the day was 2 minutes short). Deliberately does NOT touch session_close itself -- that field is also read by the frozen backtest engine (strategies/orb_intraday/engine.py) and by decide()'s own ADR-session-validity threshold, neither of which should move (strategy-passport-S021.md sec 10: 'не переоптимизировать') -- this is a live-only operational safety margin, computed in minutes (no new datetime imports needed). 19/19 tests/bot/test_orb_*.py pass unchanged. (2) New scripts/position_audit.py: reads every open broker position via the existing CTraderS007/CTraderORB.open_positions()/close_position() methods (no new order-sending code -- reuses the same path the live strategies already use) and closes anything still open, for S007 (account_strategy id=1) and S021 (id=5) only -- explicitly rejects S009/S011 (SystemExit) since those are multi-day/portfolio strategies where an open position before session start is the NORMAL resting state, not a defect. Relies on a timing invariant instead of per-strategy timezone/date arithmetic: scheduled to run 5 minutes BEFORE each strategy's own session opens (see deployment/schedule.yml's two new task entries, s007_position_audit at 09:55 Kyiv and s021_position_audit at 13:55 UTC via tz:UTC), so 'any position still open at audit time' is stale by construction -- no label/date parsing needed, which sidesteps S007 (Europe/Bucharest-anchored labels) vs S021 (fixed UTC-5-anchored labels) using different date references. 4 new tests (tests/scripts/test_position_audit.py, DB and adapter classes monkeypatched, no real broker/DB touched): scope-guard rejection, clean state closes nothing, a stale S021 position gets closed, S007 uses the right adapter class. algo-worker:latest rebuilt (`podman compose build worker`) so both the exit-buffer fix and the new audit task are live from the next scheduled tick -- verified via full test suite (scheduler_tick + bot: 147/147 pass) before the rebuild.

Fixed a real safety gap in scripts/position_audit.py (added earlier this session) caught by Anton before it ran live: audit_account_strategy() called client.open_positions() and closed EVERY position it returned, with no check on which strategy actually owns each one. S007 and S021 share the SAME cTrader account (ctrader-47939312) -- so S007's pre-session audit (09:55 Kyiv) could have closed a still-open S021 position it happened to see there, and vice versa, neither one aware it was reaching into a sibling strategy's territory. Fixed: partition open_positions() into own/foreign by label prefix (every label this codebase writes is '<MAGIC>:<date>:<...>', so 'label.startswith(f"{strategy_name}:")' is exact) -- only 'own' positions get closed; any 'foreign' one is left completely untouched but still logged loudly (ERROR, not silently skipped) so a human sees it. New test test_does_not_touch_a_sibling_strategys_position asserts an S021 audit run against a mixed S021+S007-labeled position list closes only the S021 one. Full suite: 5/5 pass (was 4/4 before this fix). algo-worker:latest rebuilt again so this fix is live before tomorrow's first scheduled audit runs (09:55 Kyiv / 13:55 UTC).

Fixed a log-directory mismatch found live 2026-09-24: scripts/position_audit.py keyed its StrategyLogger group by acc.label ('ctrader-47939312'), while webapp/runner.py's own _worker_s007/_worker_orb key theirs by acc.external_account_id or acc.id ('47939312') -- so the first two scheduled audit runs today (09:55 and 16:55 Kyiv) silently wrote into brand-new reports/logs/S007-acctctrader-47939312/ and S021-acctctrader-47939312/ directories instead of the live workers' own S007-acct47939312/ and S021-acct47939312/, fragmenting the audit trail into a second, disconnected location. Both runs themselves were correct (position_audit_clean, 0 closed -- Anton had already closed the stale S021 position from the prior incident by hand before the 16:55 run), only the log destination was wrong. (1) NEW bot/clients/ctrader/auth.py -- Twisted-free OAuth2 token layer: TokenBundle (access/refresh/expires_at, needs_refresh() with REFRESH_LEEWAY_S=3600, as_credentials()/from_credentials()), authorization_url(), exchange_authorization_code(), refresh_access_token() (handles the broker ROTATING the refresh token, keeps the old one when the answer omits it), is_expired_token_error(). Endpoints are the real ones (GET https://openapi.ctrader.com/apps/token with QUERY params, id.ctrader.com authorize) and now live in exactly one place. A missing or unparseable token_expires_at is deliberately treated as 'expires now' -- a needless refresh is cheap, a wrong 'still valid' is an outage. (2) bot/clients/ctrader/client.py substantially refactored. It was structurally broken and had never been imported by anything: every public method ran its own reactor.run(), but a Twisted reactor can only run once per OS process, so the SECOND call in a process was impossible. Now the reactor runs ONCE on a module-level daemon thread (_ensure_reactor_running, installSignalHandlers=False, guarded by reactor._startedBefore -- NOT _stopped, which is True before the reactor has ever run) and every public method is a synchronous wrapper over threads.blockingCallFromThread. Each operation is split into a _xxx_step() returning a Deferred plus a thin public wrapper via _call/_blocking_call (CALL_TIMEOUT_S=60, CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S=90), so composite flows cost ONE connect/auth. Added open()/close()/__enter__/__exit__, session-level symbol caching (the old design re-downloaded the whole symbol list on every single call), resolve_symbols()/get_symbols_details()/get_trendbars_many() for portfolio strategies, place_stop_order, and notional= + notional_price= sizing alongside volume_lots= so both the lot-sizing (S007/S021) and dollar-weight (S011) strategies are served by the same methods. Token refresh is PRE-FLIGHT (_ensure_fresh_token runs before the reactor is touched), never retry-on-failure -- a session that dies on an expired token cannot be retried in the same process. close() deliberately does NOT stop the reactor (it cannot be restarted; stopping would break every later client in the process).
